topics.title: Weekend Drinking, Bathroom Renovations, and Threats
topics.summary: During a weekend gathering, several individuals consume excessive alcohol while one undertakes an ill-advised bathroom renovation. Conversations involve financial difficulties, failed artistic endeavors, threats made by a mentally unstable individual previously arrested for threatening political figures, and discussions about media coverage of his arrest.

topics.title: Carvin Threatens Reagan, Investigation
topics.summary: Michael Carvin was investigated after threatening Ronald Reagan outside a Miami rally and sending letters with disturbing content. Tom Chiesano declined to discuss the matter due to reluctance from others involved, highlighting concerns about potential threats and documented mail sent by Carvin.

topics.title: Radio Hosts Discuss Tragedy and Personal Reflections
topics.summary: The broadcast features extended discussions among hosts about various topics, including concerns over typing speed and spelling errors, comparisons to celebrities like Mariah Carey and Warren Beatty, and reflections on the events surrounding Ben Walker’s death. Several individuals offer commentary regarding school trauma and organ donation.

topics.title: Funeral Song & Shooting at Thurston High
topics.summary: During a funeral service, callers request Metallica’s “Nothing Else Matters” to be played. Later, Howard discusses the shooting at Thurston High School in Springfield involving Jake Riker and Kip Kinkle, with details about Riker's reaction and initial reports from witnesses.

topics.title: Charlie Sheen Discusses 'Fear and Loathing'
topics.summary: During this segment, Charlie Sheen discusses his reservations about the movie "Fear and Loating," shifting to opinions on Jim Carrey’s performance in "The Truman Show" before concluding with a discussion of Robert Plant's reaction to Puff Daddy’s cover of Led Zeppelin’s “Cashmere.” 54 words

topics.title: Bathroom Shenanigans & Disturbing Archives
topics.summary: During a discussion about movie soundtracks, the conversation unexpectedly shifts to Jackie’s obsession with collecting disturbing images from online archives. He describes unsettling imagery including executions and electrocutions of children before detailing his son's discovery of these materials, alongside discussions regarding old Beatles music played loudly in a bathroom setting.
